title: How noisy is one round? About ±100-150 points
text: Mini-AlphaZero has been paused since 05:35, so every round since then used the exact same network. Its rating still went 2183, 2229, 2321, 2064. With 20 games per pair and one pinned bot, a single round moves all ratings by roughly ±100-150 together. That's why the knockouts use a three-round average and the catch-up rule a two-round average, and why the order between models matters more than any single number. Knockout 1 (12:00), three-round average now: NEAT 1865, CMA-ES 1788.

Expectation: a few rounds to show; success = beating the territory bot more often than the 20-30% PPO and DQN manage now.

title: Change 2 for CMA-ES: restart its search
text: Playing against the rivals (change 1, 00:39) didn't help in three rounds: 1662, 1689, 1592. The real problem showed in its log: the step size had shrunk from 0.19 (generation 650) to 0.004, so each generation only tried networks almost identical to the current one. The search had frozen. Standard CMA-ES remedy: a restart. It keeps the current best weights as the centre but resets the step size to 0.3 and forgets the learned covariance, so it explores again. The rival opponents stay. Expectation: worse for a round or two, then up if there's anything left to find in a 23-32-3 network. The knockout is in 9 hours.

title: Restart after a bug in the supervisor
text: In the first few minutes the supervisor couldn't see its own trainers (its process pattern started with '-m', which the pgrep tool reads as an option), so every 20 seconds it started another copy of all five. After 3 minutes about 50 trainers were fighting over 8 cores and the same files. Fixed (the pattern is anchored on the full interpreter path, and the supervisor now refuses to run two trainers for one model), all runs were wiped, and the tournament restarted from scratch at 22:07.

title: Training has started
text: All five trainers passed a 2-minute smoke test (PPO ~2,000 steps/s, DQN ~1,000 steps/s, NEAT ~15 s per generation of 120, CMA-ES ~4 s per generation of 32, Mini-AlphaZero ~1,200 self-play games per hour, each on one core). A test ranking round with 2-minute-old models already put the tree-search model level with the space-filler bot: search with a perfect model of the game is a big head start. Each model now gets one pinned core (cores 0-4); cores 5-7 run ranking rounds and this website.

title: The tournament is being built
text: Wednesday evening: the Tron simulator (30x30 board, numba) and this website go up first so you can follow along. Next: the five trainers (PPO, DQN, NEAT, CMA-ES, Mini-AlphaZero), the ranking rounds and the supervisor that runs the catch-up rule and the knockouts. Training starts as soon as every model passes a 5-minute sanity test.
